metadata.body:
# PoroTomo Induced-Seismicity Agent

Blueprint for clio-agent. The numeric work lives in plain scripts in this
repository so it can run on PBS compute nodes without an LLM:

- `agent/manifest.py`: list the DASV records on `s3://nrel-pds-porotomo/` and sample them.
- `agent/detect.py`: per-record detector (common-mode removal, 10-150 Hz band-pass, median STA/LTA).
- `agent/pbs/submit.sh`: submit the distributed detection plus aggregation job to Aurora.
- `agent/hazard.py`: anomaly z-scores, event catalogue, pumping volumes, seismogenic index, probabilities.

The experts orchestrate those scripts, inspect files, and explain results. They
never make up numbers. Every figure they report comes from `summary.json` or a
tool result.

Install by linking this directory into `~/.config/clio-agent/agent-blueprints/`.

agent_blueprint.name: PoroTomo Induced-Seismicity Agent

session.title: porotomo-induced-seismicity: Report the headline results of the agent

answer:
Headline results of the agent run at /home/hyoklee/poro/agent/results/run_20261115T155359Z_s20 (read-only inspection of the existing outputs; no PBS jobs submitted, hazard.py not run). All numbers below are quoted exactly from summary.json (generated 2026-11-15T16:02:33+00:00) and independently re-verified from the per-record files (detect/detect_rank0000..0047.jsonl + detect_retry_login.jsonl, events.csv, anomalies.csv, hourly.csv).

SCOPE OF THE RUN
- Source: PoroTomo DAS .h5 records at Brady Hot Springs, March 2016. manifest.log: 15,164 total records available; 759 selected at stride 20 (every 20th record, one per ~10 min), covering 2016-03-18T02:09:17Z to 2016-03-26T00:59:44Z (an 8-day window inside the 2016-03-11 to 2016-03-27 pumping period; sampled_fraction_of_time = 0.033141355084075994, i.e. only ~3.3% of the time was recorded). Detection ran as PBS job 9092130 (2 nodes x 24 ranks = 48 ranks, finished in 188 s); 6 initial download_failed records were retried and all ended 'ok'.

COUNTS
- Records analysed: 759 (records.analysed = 759; by_status {ok: 759}; 759 unique record keys in the detect/*.jsonl shards).
- Anomalous records: 57 (anomalies.n_anomalous = 57 at z_threshold = 5.0; anomalies.csv has 57 data rows; top anomaly zmax = 30.92 on 2016-03-23T20:50:17Z, driver max_sta_lta).
- DAS detections: 62 events (das_events.n = 62) across 53 records with events (das_events.records_with_events = 53); 62 rows in events.csv; das_events.n_scaled_to_full_time = 1870.77; 34 detections above the relative completeness magnitude mc_relative = -0.8492463451632817; relative b (Aki MLE) = 0.9849352475487246.

SEISMOGENIC INDEX Sigma AND P(Mw>=5.5) PER YEAR — CALIBRATED (LBNL catalogue)
From summary.json "hazard_catalog_based", calibrated against the LBNL/NCEDC March 2016 catalogue (catalog.source = "GDR 859, LBNL/NCEDC March 2016", n = 5 ML events, mc = -0.48, mag_max = 0.07). These are the CALIBRATED probabilities. P(Mw>=5.5) per year is the "p_per_year_at_observed_rate" field:
- b = 1.0: Sigma = -5.448901270028832; P(Mw>=5.5)/yr = 0.00011982478978644906 (~1.20e-4 per year)
- b = 0.73: Sigma = -5.3193012700288325; P(Mw>=5.5)/yr = 0.004921548824626587 (~4.92e-3 per year)
- b = 0.65: Sigma = -5.280901270028833; P(Mw>=5.5)/yr = 0.014735103451029574 (~1.47e-2 per year)
(For reference, the same scenarios also give P(Mw>=5.5) over the observed volume of 5.235629034316958e-06, 0.00021553767643867072, and 0.0006483793467004784, and P if the Pohang injected volume of 1.4398215464339614e-07, 5.927989317755511e-06, 1.7836302385054736e-05.)

DAS-BASED UPPER BOUND — UNCALIBRATED
From summary.json "hazard_das_upper_bound" (b_used = 0.9849352475487246 from the DAS relative-magnitude Aki MLE; b_source = "DAS relative-magnitude Aki MLE"):
- Sigma = -2.698279919032152
- P(Mw>=5.5)/yr at observed rate = 0.07842182774171746 (~7.8e-2 per year)
This is an UPPER BOUND with UNCALIBRATED magnitudes: it treats every DAS detection as an event at or above the catalogue minimum magnitude, so it OVER-COUNTS. It is NOT the calibrated estimate and must not be quoted as one.

WHICH IS WHICH
- The CALIBRATED probability is the LBNL/NCEDC catalogue-based one ("hazard_catalog_based"): Sigma -5.45 to -5.28 and P(Mw>=5.5)/yr of 1.20e-4 to 1.47e-2 per year across b = 1.0/0.73/0.65.
- The DAS-based number (Sigma = -2.698279919032152, P(Mw>=5.5)/yr = 0.07842182774171746) is an uncalibrated UPPER BOUND with uncalibrated (relative) magnitudes.

ASSUMPTIONS EACH NUMBER RESTS ON (as stated in the run files)
- 759-record count: stride-20 sampling of 15,164 records (~3.3% of the time), so rare events could be missed; 8-day window only (2016-03-18 to 2016-03-26) within a 16-day pumping window (GDR 917 corrected deployment data; injected 465,448 m3, extracted 505,933 m3, net injected -40,485 m3).
- Anomalies: z-score threshold 5.0 on per-record features (drivers mainly max_sta_lta, some spectral_centroid_hz / n_events).
- Calibrated Sigma/P: rely on a very small local catalogue (only 5 ML events, mc = -0.48) and the assumed b-values (1.0, 0.73, 0.65); model P = 1 - exp(-V 10^(Sigma - b M)) (Shapiro et al. 2021 Eq. 5).
- DAS upper bound: extrapolates from limited DAS-derived relative magnitudes (Aki MLE b = 0.9849) and over-counts by treating every detection as >= the catalogue minimum magnitude; magnitudes are uncalibrated.
- Sigma uncertainty is wide (-5.45 to -2.70) and strongly changes the probabilities; the site Sigma needed for a 1% Mw>=5.5 probability over the observed volume is -2.17 (b=1.0), -3.65 (b=0.73), -4.09 (b=0.65) — i.e. the calibrated site values are far below that.
- Hourly Spearman correlations of events vs net injection are weak (-0.1728; vs abs change in net -0.0296; vs injection -0.0926) and cannot establish causality.

Note: interpretation.md contains a stale "Calibration note" calling the DAS bound calibrated; the reviewer note and the summary.json field names ("hazard_catalog_based" vs "hazard_das_upper_bound") give the correct labeling used above.
